paper_title: AttentionInfluence Adopting Attention Head Influence for Weak-to-Strong   Pretraining Data Selection
caption: The statistics of clustering. The left is the clustering result of AttentionInfluence, the right part is that of FineWeb-Edu Classifier.
model_annotation: The image displays two donut charts side by side, illustrating the clustering statistics of two different methods: AttentionInfluence (left) and FineWeb-Edu Classifier (right). Each chart is divided into multiple colored segments, with labels and numerical values indicating the proportion or count of each category. In the AttentionInfluence chart, the largest segment is "Education" at 25, followed by "Teaching & resources" at 15, "Health & Medicine" at 22, and "History & Society" at 23. Other notable segments include "Science & technology education" (10), "Diseases" (11), "Animal & Plant" (13), and "Society & culture" (10). Smaller segments include "Materials" (2), "Emerging tech" (4), "Policy" (1), and "Manage" (2). The FineWeb-Edu Classifier chart shows a different distribution, with "Education" being the largest at 38, followed by "Teaching & resources" (17), "Science & technology education" (19), and "Health & Medicine" (19). Other segments include "History & Society" (19), "Historical review" (12), "Animal & Plant" (12), "Diseases" (10), and "Nutrition" (7). Smaller segments are "Materials" (3), "Events & people" (2), "Society & culture" (5), "Emerging tech" (4), "Manage" (1), and "Healthy education" (2). Both charts use a similar color scheme and layout, with labels pointing to each segment, and the FineWeb-Edu Classifier chart includes a small "..." segment indicating additional, unlisted categories. The overall visual structure suggests a comparison of how each method categorizes or clusters data, with noticeable differences in the proportions of certain categories, particularly in the dominance of "Education" and "Teaching & resources" in the FineWeb-Edu Classifier.
